@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos21

/-- An Erdős–Lovász family of order `n`: an intersecting family of `n`-sets such that every set
of size at most `n - 1` is disjoint from some member. -/
def IsErdosLovaszFamily (n : ℕ) (F : Finset (Finset ℕ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ A ∈ F, A.card = n) ∧ (∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, (A ∩ B).Nonempty) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.card ≤ n - 1 → ∃ A ∈ F, Disjoint S A

/-- `f n` is the minimal size of an Erdős–Lovász family of order `n`. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | ∃ F : Finset (Finset ℕ), IsErdosLovaszFamily n F ∧ F.card = m}

/--
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that there is an intersecting family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets of size $n$
(so $A\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for all $A,B\in \mathcal{F}$) with $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=f(n)$
such that any set $S$ with $\lvert S\rvert \leq n-1$ is disjoint from at least one
$A\in \mathcal{F}$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) \ll n?$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75], who proved that
$$\frac{8}{3}n-3\leq f(n) \ll n^{3/2}\log n$$
for all $n$. The upper bound was improved by Kahn [Ka92b] to $f(n) \ll n\log n$. (The upper
bound constructions in both cases are formed by taking a random set of lines from a projective
plane of order $n-1$, assuming $n-1$ is a prime power.)

This problem was solved by Kahn [Ka94] who proved the upper bound $f(n) \ll n$. The Erdős-Lovász
lower bound of $\frac{8}{3}n-O(1)$ has not been improved, and it has been speculated (see e.g.
[Ka94]) that the correct answer is $3n+O(1)$.

It is trivial that $f(1)=1$ and $f(2)=3$. The values $f(3)=6$ and $f(4)=9$ were established by
Tripathi [Tr14]. Barát and Wanless [BaWa21] proved that $f(5)=13$, and that $13\leq f(6)\leq 18$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at

theorem erdos_21 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, f n ≤ C * n := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75] proved that $\frac{8}{3}n-3\leq f(n)$ for all $n$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_21.variants.lower (n : ℕ) : (8 / 3 : ℝ) * n - 3 ≤ f n := by
  sorry

/-- It has been speculated (see e.g. [Ka94]) that the correct answer is $3n+O(1)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_21.variants.three_n : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    f n ≤ 3 * n + C ∧ 3 * n ≤ f n + C := by
  sorry

/-- $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=3$, $f(3)=6$ [Tr14], $f(4)=9$ [Tr14] and $f(5)=13$ [BaWa21]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_21.variants.small_values : f 1 = 1 ∧ f 2 = 3 ∧ f 3 = 6 ∧ f 4 = 9 ∧ f 5 = 13 := by
  sorry

end Erdos21

findings.description: The [BaWa21] reference at lines 41–42 has the wrong author list and page range. The cited paper is by János Barát alone, not Barát and Wanless, and appears on pages 193–209, not 260–286. The same incorrect joint attribution occurs in the docstring of Erdos21.erdos_21. The stated small values are nevertheless correct.
findings.source_evidence: The title page of arXiv:2011.04444 names only János Barát. Its theorem on the 5-uniform case establishes the minimum of 13 edges. The publisher's metadata for DOI 10.1002/jcd.21763 identifies János Barát as the sole author and gives Journal of Combinatorial Designs 29(3) (2021), 193–209. Sivashankar's 2026 paper independently cites these same bibliographic details.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the reference to J. Barát, Journal of Combinatorial Designs 29(3) (2021), 193–209, DOI 10.1002/jcd.21763, and credit Barát alone in the main theorem's docstring. Update the reference key consistently if desired; no mathematical statement needs changing.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open] with answer(sorry). The main theorem's background also says that the 8n/3-O(1) lower bound has not been improved.
status_issues.source_status: The speculation is disproved by Varun Sivashankar's 2026 lower bound. The source discussion reports the June 2026 improvement. The current paper, arXiv:2606.24878v2 (July 29, 2026), Theorem 1(ii), proves f(n) ≥ ((41-√19)/12-ε)n for every ε>0 and all sufficiently large n. Since (41-√19)/12>3, f(n)-3n grows at least linearly and cannot be O(1).
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24878 and its LaTeX source, Theorem 1(ii), define exactly the minimum number of edges in an intersecting n-uniform hypergraph with covering number n. The archived source discussion at https://web.archive.org/web/20260804000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/21 contains the June 24, 2026 report of the earlier 61/20-o(1) coefficient. Both coefficients exceed 3.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change three_n to category research solved and answer(False), leaving its right-hand side unchanged. Cite Sivashankar's result and update the background paragraph that says the original lower bound has not been improved. The original lower-bound theorem remains correct.

reformulations.difference: The source's Vinogradov bound f(n) ≪ n is expressed using a natural-number constant and an eventual inequality rather than real-valued big-O notation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both f(n) and n are nonnegative. A natural-number bound gives the corresponding real norm bound directly; conversely, any real big-O constant can be increased to a natural number. The eventual quantifier is precisely the sufficiently-large-n quantifier in big-O. A generic equivalence for every function ℕ → ℕ was proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's f(n) = 3n + O(1) is represented by the two natural-number inequalities f n ≤ 3*n + C and 3*n ≤ f n + C.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: After casting to ℝ, the conjunction is equivalent to |f(n) - 3n| ≤ C. Existence of an eventual natural-number bound is equivalent to existence of a real bound by rounding upward. Thus the right-hand side states exactly that f(n) - 3n is O(1), not merely f(n) = O(n) or f(n)/n → 3. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the six declarations. Independent Lean checks established existence and attainment of the minimum for every n>0, f 0 = 0, f 1 = 1, and equivalence with the covering-number formulation. The zero default is harmless for all stated claims. Computations verified 3-, 6-, 9-, and 13-edge witnesses for orders 2–5. A further Lean lemma verifies that an eventual lower bound with coefficient strictly above 3 refutes three_n. Experiments are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file is unchanged. Live erdosproblems.com requests were blocked, so archived source pages were used. Er90 and Er97f chapter texts were inaccessible; their overlapping claim was checked against the other primary sources. The linked formal proof's definitions and final theorem match the repository statement; its separate project was not rebuilt to audit all transitive axioms.
